purpose: Plain-language CBT 95 glossary for human navigation and teaching. Definitions are educational context, not diagnostic criteria or standalone medical evidence.

terms.definition: A thought or interpretation that appears quickly in response to a situation. CBT may make it explicit so it can be examined rather than automatically treated as fact.
An interpretation that tries to fit the available evidence without forced positivity or unnecessary catastrophe.
A planned, safe, low-stakes observation used to test a specific prediction against what actually happens.
The teaching model used here: situation, thought or interpretation, emotion and body response, behaviour, then consequence or feedback.
Reconsidering how a situation is interpreted while preserving relevant facts and uncertainty.

The kind of evidence a record represents, such as a guideline recommendation, randomized trial, systematic review, public education, or archived guidance. CBT 95 does not collapse these into one universal ranking.
A working explanation of how situations, interpretations, emotions, behaviours and consequences may be linked. A formulation is not automatically a diagnosis or proof of cause.
A recommendation issued by an identified guideline body within a stated population and jurisdiction. It is not individualized medical advice.
Educational or structured CBT-style material used outside clinician-delivered treatment. It is not automatically equivalent to assessment or therapy delivered by a qualified practitioner.
A care principle in which treatment options, benefits, risks, limitations and preferences are discussed so the person can participate in decisions.
A versioned metadata record showing what source identity and status CBT 95 verified at a particular time. It is not a copy of the remote full text.

A record preserving relevant evidence differences instead of averaging them into a synthetic consensus. Scope, jurisdiction, intervention, comparator, outcome, authority or currency may explain the difference.
